title: Kernel selector v2: document rollback switch + tighten override precedence defaults
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Internal-only: clarified selector v2 rollback/override behavior in-code; safer defaults to prevent accidental v2 enablement and to make kill switch precedence explicit.
description: Context: during the staged rollout work for kernel auto-selection v2 we’ve had a few close calls where (a) the kill switch semantics weren’t obvious from the config structs, and (b) it wasn’t clear which setting wins when multiple override mechanisms are present (global selector version flag, per-model-family pin, emergency safe-kernel-set, and legacy v1 fallback). This PR does two things: (1) adds inline documentation and examples next to the config/flag definitions so oncall can reason about rollback quickly under pressure, and (2) tightens defaults + precedence so we fail closed (v1) and ensure the emergency rollback switch always wins. Changes: Document precedence order explicitly in the config types and in the selector decision path; Make selector_v2_enabled default false unless explicitly set (prevents accidental enablement on new regions/clusters inheriting partial config); Rename internal fields for clarity (no external API changes) and add validation warnings in logs when conflicting settings are detected; Add unit tests covering precedence (kill switch > safe kernel set > per-family override > table-driven v2 > v1) and a regression test for the "unset config" path; Add a small trace annotation when an override path is taken (sampled; no new high-cardinality labels). Rollout/compat: This is a behavior-preserving change for clusters that already set selector_v2_enabled explicitly. For clusters relying on implicit defaults (rare; mostly internal dev), v2 will no longer come on unless enabled. This is intentional and aligns with SRE guardrails. Testing: unit tests + config validation tests; ran runtime-integration test suite; no benchmark changes expected. Follow-ups: We should link the oncall runbook section for override usage from Console docs (out of scope here).

conversation: Grace Kim (review): Thanks for doing this—this has been confusing in the last two canary toggles. Two asks: (1) can we make the precedence order show up right next to the config keys (not only in selector code) and (2) can we add a test that ensures per-family overrides do NOT bypass safe kernel set (we had that concern in the NaN thread)?

Benji Okafor (author): Good call. I moved the precedence diagram into selector_flags.h next to the config key docs and added kernel_selector_override_precedence_test coverage for safe-kernel-set winning over per-family pins. Also added an explicit comment in the selector path where we gate pins behind safe-kernel-set when enabled.

Allison Grant (review): Please confirm the trace annotation won’t explode cardinality. What are the allowed values? Also, any chance we can include the reason string in logs but keep traces as a small enum?

Benji Okafor (author): Yep. Trace annotation is a small enum: {kill_switch, safe_set, per_family, v2_table, v1_fallback}. No model name, no kernel id. Logs (warn) include which keys conflicted, but we avoid including raw model identifiers. Sampling is 1% at the span level and only when override path != v2_table.

Connor O'Brien (review): Release perspective: defaulting v2 off is great, but we need to be explicit about which config key changed behavior. Are we changing the external config surface or only internal defaults? Also, can you add a one-liner in the release notes fragment so oncall knows to look here during rollback?

Benji Okafor (author): External config keys unchanged. Behavior change is only when selector_v2_enabled is unset (previously some clusters effectively treated unset as true via inherited defaults; now unset -> false). I added a short internal release note line in the runtime changelog section and expanded comments in selector_flags.h with the exact key names used in prod config.

Omar El-Sayed (review): Nit: In kernel_selector_v2.cc, the function explainDecision() still shows v2_table as the default path even when kill switch is active; should that reflect the early exit? This is used by the debug endpoint in PR 18507.
Benji Okafor (author): Great catch. Fixed so explainDecision mirrors the actual precedence (kill switch -> safe set -> per-family -> v2/v1). Added a unit test for explain output as well.
Grace Kim (review): Re-ran the tests locally; looks good. Approved.
Allison Grant (review): Approved once the sampling note is in the comment (so future edits don’t accidentally remove it).
Benji Okafor (author): Added sampling note and linked to telemetry standards doc in a comment. Thanks!
Connor O'Brien (review): Approved. Please coordinate merge timing with the rollout checklist so we don’t have mixed semantics between regions.
Benji Okafor (author): Will do—queued for today’s runtime train; will ping in #eng-releases after merge.
